title: PhaseNet catalog reveals a 2023 injection-linked earthquake cluster in the Raton Basin
summary: Applying PhaseNet-based phase picking to eight years of recordings from eight broadband stations, the study built a roughly 96,000-event Raton Basin catalog (local magnitudes −1 to 4.3) and resolved a previously unreported 2023 cluster with a Mw 4.3 event. Nearby wells had elevated injection volumes for about a year before the cluster; analysis of relocated events and 90 full centroid moment tensors also supports basement-rooted normal faults and possible elevated pore pressure. The authors interpret injection as a likely influence, not a demonstrated sole cause.
ai_technology: PhaseNet deep neural-network seismic phase picker in the LOC-FLOW workflow
organization: Southern University of Science and Technology; University of New Mexico; U.S. Geological Survey

evidence.tested: Applying PhaseNet-based phase picking to eight years of recordings from eight broadband stations, the study built a roughly 96,000-event Raton Basin catalog (local magnitudes −1 to 4.3) and resolved a previously unreported 2023 cluster with a Mw 4.3 event.
evidence.unknown: The authors report an association between nearby injection and seismicity and infer elevated pore pressure from positive isotropic components; this does not establish injection as the sole cause. They note possible residual isotropic-component artifacts from velocity heterogeneity or noise and explicitly limit interpretation of CLVD components. The paper gives slightly inconsistent catalog totals: 95,993 in the abstract and most text, but 95,933 in one discussion passage; this summary therefore says roughly 96,000. The newly resolved cluster is distinct from earlier Raton Basin seismicity studies cited by the authors.
evidence.ai_role: PhaseNet picked P and S arrivals directly from continuous waveforms at eight broadband stations, including four stations not telemetered for routine cataloging. These picks enabled event association, relocation, and the expanded 2016–2024 catalog used to identify and analyze the 2023 cluster. PhaseNet enabled the denser earthquake observations; the injection comparison and full-CMT mechanism analysis were subsequent statistical and geophysical analyses.
